story:
Ava skipped into her classroom, her favorite purple backpack bouncing. Today was "Jungle Adventure Mural Day"! Mrs. Davis explained, "We are making a giant, colorful jungle, and everyone will paint a special part." Ava felt a little **nervous** but also very excited. She loved drawing animals, especially bright green parrots and spotted jaguars. She **thought** about all the different animals she could draw. Her goal was to make her part of the mural the most amazing jungle section.

Mrs. Davis handed Ava a big piece of paper. "Ava, you get the tall, leafy trees and some **curious** monkeys swinging high," she said. Ava looked at the paper. It was much bigger than she **thought**. She wanted to paint a big, beautiful tree, but it felt hard to reach the top. She tried to stretch, holding her paintbrush high, but the branch she wanted to paint was still too far. A small frown touched her face. She felt a bit **frustrated** because she couldn't reach the **highest** part of her paper.

"Need some help?" a friendly voice asked. It was Leo, who sat at the next table. He had a big smile. "My paper has a wide river, but I can help you with your tall tree, **so that** we can both finish." Ava looked at Leo, then at her tall paper. "Yes, please," she said. "The tree is very tall." Leo pulled his chair closer. "We can **share** the paint and **take turns** reaching," he suggested. "I can paint the very top leaves, and you can paint the big brown trunk and the bright red flowers." Ava smiled. "That's a good idea! I can paint a big, **curly** vine, too, **because** monkeys love to swing on them."

They started to paint. Leo painted green leaves at the very top, and Ava carefully painted the **sturdy** brown tree trunk. They **listened** to Mrs. Davis's directions about mixing colors. "Why do you think the monkeys are curious?" Leo asked. "Maybe **because** they see a yummy banana **under** a big leaf," Ava replied, giggling. They kept painting, carefully adding more details. When Leo needed to paint a **darker** shade of green, Ava handed him the blue paint to mix. "You can **try again** to make it darker," she said.

Soon, Ava and Leo's section of the mural looked amazing! There was a towering tree with **glossy** leaves, and **playful** monkeys swinging on curly vines. Ava had painted a bright yellow banana **next to** a **fuzzy** brown monkey. She felt a wave of **relief** that they had finished it together, and very **proud** of their beautiful work. Mrs. Davis came over. "What a wonderful jungle section, Ava and Leo! You worked so well together." Ava felt **grateful** for Leo's help. "It was fun to **share** and paint with Leo," she said, looking at her friend. Leo nodded. "Yes, we made a great team." They carefully put their finished art onto the big classroom mural. It looked like a real jungle now, full of colorful animals and tall, green trees.
